title: The Lalitavistara — the Sanskrit text
textType: Mahayana sutra in prose and verse
attributionNote: A Mahayana sutra on the life of the Buddha, transmitted without an author: the Sarvāstivāda life of the Buddha elaborated with the Bodhisattva's career and the pure lands, and read as scripture rather than as biography. GRETIL's e-text follows P. L. Vaidya's edition (Darbhanga 1958, Buddhist Sanskrit Texts 1) and was input by the Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon Input Project.
description: The Lalitavistara tells the Buddha's life as a cosmic play: the descent from the Tuṣita heaven, the conception and the dream of Māyā, the birth in Lumbinī and the terrestrial signs, the childhood and the lessons that outran his teachers, the women of the palace, the four encounters, the departure, the six years of asceticism, the defeat of Māra, the awakening, and the sermons of the first turning and of the great assembly at Varanasi, closing with the Bodhisattva's vows and the cosmic audiences that surround them — the fullest biography of the Buddha in the Sanskrit canon of the Mahayana.
historicalContext: The text took its present form in the centuries around the turn of the era and was translated into Chinese in the third century and into Tibetan soon after; it shaped Buddhist art from Gandhara to Borobudur, and is the source through which the Buddha's life was told as scripture rather than as legend.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: all twenty-seven parivartas, 1,515 passages of prose and verse, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
